Where vehicles or transport operations fall outside the scope of Regulation 561/2006, your country is free to make its own rules for them, and those rules may copy the EU rules or simply be inspired by them. The Commission confirmed this when Germany applied the EU rules to vehicles over 2.8 tonnes. That note dates from 1993 and is older than the current Regulation. Under the current Regulation, goods vehicles generally fall under the EU rules only above 3,5 tonnes. However, from 1 July 2026 the EU rules apply directly to vehicles over 2,5 tonnes used in international transport or cabotage. So a 2.8-tonne van on those trips will be covered by EU law itself, not just by national rules. National transport with such vans remains outside EU scope, so your country may still regulate it.

{"answerable": true, "answer": "You must write the symbol of the country you are entering at the start of your first stop in that Member State. That stop must be at the nearest possible stopping place at or after the border. If you cross on a ferry or train, write it at the port or station of arrival.

The Commission guidance gives three places on the disc, in this order:
1. **First choice:** under the inner time dial, just underneath the time at which you stopped after the border. If you opened the tachograph and a reference line was marked, put the code under that line. You don't need to add the date or time, because the disc already shows them.
